newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas untraded again, second blank day runnin.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas untraded again, second blank day runnin.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures contract was untraded for the second day running on Tuesday.

Front month August was offered at 9.40 pence a therm by the close of the two-hour afternoon session, although the bid was withdrawn a few seconds before the market closed. The offer was down from the previous settlement price of 9.45 pence a therm.

Only two bids were posted at all by the close of trade, in November at 12.40 pence and in March at 13.00 pence. Both these months also saw offers, although in the case of March the bid/offer spread of 1.35 pence a therm was so wide as to make trade seem an extremely remote possibility.
Only four offers were posted, in August, October, November and March.

IPE gas activity has been erratic since it started at the end of January, with periods of relatively active trade interspersed with periods when nothing is done at all. The exchange recently announced a number of changes to the contract, taking effect on August 8, which are designed to boost liquidity.
